::: proof
We sketch the argument for a scalar parameter
and the point null hypothesis $H_0: \th = \th_0$,
which imposes $q = 1$ constraint.
Then the restricted MLE is $\hat\th_0 = \th_0$, and
$\Lambda = 2\paren{\llik(\hthml) - \llik(\th_0)}$.
For the full proof, see [@wilks1938] or [@dobson4e, Section 5.7].

*Step 1: expand the log-likelihood around the MLE.*
The MLE maximizes $\llik$ at an interior point,
so $\score(\hthml) = 0$.
A second-order Taylor expansion of $\llik(\th_0)$ around $\hthml$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\llik(\th_0)
&\approx \llik(\hthml) + \score(\hthml)(\th_0 - \hthml)
 + \frac{1}{2}\hess(\hthml)(\th_0 - \hthml)^2
&& \text{(Taylor expansion)}\\
&= \llik(\hthml) + \frac{1}{2}\hess(\hthml)(\th_0 - \hthml)^2
&& \text{($\score(\hthml) = 0$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Rearranging:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Lambda
&= 2\paren{\llik(\hthml) - \llik(\th_0)}
&& \text{(definition of $\Lambda$)}\\
&\approx -\hess(\hthml)(\hthml - \th_0)^2
&& \text{(substitute the expansion)}\\
&= \oinf(\hthml)(\hthml - \th_0)^2
&& \text{(observed information is the negative Hessian)}
\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2: replace the observed information by the expected information.*
Under the regularity conditions,
$\oinf(\hthml)/\einf(\th_0) \to 1$ in probability,
by the law of large numbers and the consistency of $\hthml$, so:

$$\Lambda \approx \einf(\th_0)(\hthml - \th_0)^2$$

*Step 3: recognize a squared standard Gaussian variable.*
Define $Z \eqdef \sqrt{\einf(\th_0)}\,(\hthml - \th_0)$,
so that $\Lambda \approx Z^2$.
By @thm-dist-mle, $\hthml \dsim \ndist{\th_0, \einf(\th_0)^{-1}}$ under $H_0$,
so $Z \dsim \ndist{0, 1}$,
and therefore $\Lambda \approx Z^2$ has approximately a $\chi^2_1$ distribution.

With $q$ constraints, the same argument in matrix form
makes $\Lambda$ approximately a sum of $q$ squared,
independent standard Gaussian variables,
which has a $\chi^2_q$ distribution.
:::
